title: 1953 Skyways Avro York disappearance
summary: On 2 February 1953, Avro York G-AHFA departed Stansted for Jamaica via Newfoundland, carrying military personnel and families including 13 children. The aircraft transmitted position reports from departure through 04:25 on 2 February. At 05:31 Gander Radio received an urgency signal followed immediately by repeated distress signals SOS, SOS, SOS DE G-A, then silence. Extensive air and sea search located oil patches and dye markers 120 miles southwest of the last reported position but no wreckage or survivors. The cause of the loss was determined to be unascertainable.
probable_cause: Cause unascertainable. Chief Investigation Officer noted possibility of uncontrollable fire in aircraft engines, but investigation concluded the loss developed suddenly and violently without determination of specific cause.

factors.evidence: Chief Investigation Officer opinion: may have been uncontrollable fire in one of aircraft's engines
Urgency and distress signals transmitted at high speed suggesting sudden violent emergency
Aircraft lost from Gander Radio; extensive search recovered oil patches indicating catastrophic loss over ocean

title: Tachikawa air disaster
summary: A United States Air Force Douglas C-124A Globemaster II crashed on June 18, 1953, three minutes after takeoff from Tachikawa Air Base, Japan. The aircraft's No. 1 outer left engine burst into flames one minute into the flight. The commander shut down the engine and declared return to base, requesting ground-controlled approach. However, during return procedures the left wing stalled, causing the aircraft to roll left into an unrecoverable dive. The aircraft crashed into a watermelon patch 3.5 miles from the airbase, killing all 129 people aboard. The investigation determined the crash was caused by improper flap usage and airspeed loss following the port engine failure.
probable_cause: Improper flap usage and airspeed loss due to the failure of the port engine, resulting in wing stall and loss of control.

title: Transocean Air Lines 512
summary: Transocean Air Lines Flight 512, a Douglas DC-6A, disappeared over the Pacific Ocean approximately 630 kilometers east of Wake Island while en route to Honolulu. The aircraft had departed Wake Island at 06:58 GMT and missed its next scheduled position report. Another aircraft flying north of the scheduled route reported encountering an extensive thunderstorm with heavy turbulence, though the pre-departure weather briefing did not indicate significant turbulence. The fuselage was not recovered, preventing mechanical analysis.
probable_cause: Unable to determine; fuselage not recovered and no physical evidence of fire or mechanical failure could be examined.

title: Air France 178

location.name: Pelat Massif near Barcelonnette, French Alps

summary: An Air France Lockheed L-749 Constellation departed Orly at 22:00 bound for Nice on September 1, 1953. At 23:25 the crew requested descent from 13,600 feet and reported violent local storms. Approximately 5 minutes later, the aircraft struck Mont Le Cimet in the Pelat Massif about 500 feet below the summit and burst into flames, killing all 42 aboard.
